title: What is CSS? 🎨
description: Deepen your understanding of how CSS brings life to HTML, and meet the browser's default styles.

slides.title: CSS: The Designer's Toolkit 🖌️
slides.content:
# Cascading Style Sheets

CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is the language that describes the presentation of HTML documents. While HTML defines *what* content exists, CSS controls *how* it looks.

With CSS you can set:
- Colours, fonts, spacing
- Layout and positioning
- Animations and transitions
- Responsive design for different devices

Without CSS, the web would be a sea of black text on white backgrounds. CSS makes it beautiful.

slides.title: Browser Default Styles 📄
slides.content:
# Every Browser Applies Its Own Base Styles

Even a page with zero CSS doesn't look truly plain. Browsers have a **default style sheet** (user agent stylesheet) that adds:
- Headings are bold and sized differently
- Paragraphs have margins
- Links are blue and underlined
- Lists have bullets or numbers

These defaults differ slightly across browsers. CSS resets or normalizers are often used to create a consistent starting point.

slides.title: The 'Cascading' Part 🌊
slides.content:
# What Does Cascade Mean?

Styles can come from multiple sources (browser defaults, external stylesheets, inline styles) and they can **cascade** – meaning later or more specific rules override earlier ones.

Understanding the cascade is crucial. We'll explore it in detail later, but for now know that CSS reads top‑down; if two rules target the same element, the last one (with equal specificity) wins.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use Inspect Element

Right‑click any element on a webpage and choose 'Inspect' to see the CSS rules applied to it. It's the best way to learn how sites are styled.
